chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Salama ibn Muhriz, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one whom Al-Hamd does not cure, nothing would cure him'.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (asws)
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: Al-Hamd (The Praise), referring specifically to Surah Al-Fatihah
key_terms.يُبْرِئْهُ: Yubri'hu (He cures/heals him), referring to spiritual or physical healing

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Surah Al-Fatihah in curing spiritual and physical ailments according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (as) highlights Surah Al-Fatihah as the ultimate spiritual remedy, asserting that its failure to heal indicates a deeper blockage that no other cure can address. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view of Al-Fatihah not merely as a prayer, but as a comprehensive key to unlocking divine mercy and curing both physical and spiritual ailments.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bn Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Salma Bin Muhriz who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one whom (Surah) Al-Hamd (Chapter 1) does not cure, nothing would cure him’.
en.sarwar: 22. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Salmah ibn Muhriz who has said the following: “
I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘If al-Hamd, (the first Chapter of the Holy Quran) would not cure one, nothing else could cure one.’”
